scope: SEC-07/18 node-shutdown worker admission before roster transfer. Context/stack/retirement-node/master-table preparation is fallible outside coordinator/roster guards. Fresh current-LP pinning and input publication share one retained IRQ mask. Existing signatures, generic syscall rejection, agent fail-closed policy, deadlines and cleanup completion requirements are unchanged.
source_review: The baseline transfers the steady-state roster, then uses mandatory spawn_thread_on_lp. This can panic on construction/publication failure after shutdown ownership transferred. No real heap-exhaustion panic was induced. The correction uses the existing thread table and admission families, without a new production registry.
native_controls: Invalid phase grace and an existing coordinator reject without running the preparation callback.
Injected preparation failure runs outside coordinator/roster guards and leaves roster/coordinator/deadline unchanged.
Actual prepared kernel thread with abort admission fenced rejects before queue mutation; its exact generation is cancelled and roster remains present.
Absent roster cancels the actual unstarted preparation without dispatch.
A deterministic winner installed between precheck and commit leaves the loser unstarted/cancelled and preserves the roster.
Abandoning a prepared receipt beneath actual root/thread-table/heap guards leaves its exact table-owned payload in NeedsLpAssignment.
Successful first dispatch observes the committed coordinator and stable original deadline; duplicate start prepares no second worker.
Each fixture preserves its incoming IRQ state. Bounded atomic observation is fixture-only, establishes no quiescence and authorizes no release.
retention_limit: Each isolated fixture deliberately retains one abandoned kernel-thread context, sixteen-page kernel stack and retirement-node charge in the real master table. It never reconstructs that abandoned receipt for cleanup. This is terminal retention, not recovery custody.

pre_boot_failures.classification: Host signing subprocess received SIGKILL before kernel build or guest entry. Cause unconfirmed; no complete failed bundle snapshot retained. The passing Intel repeat is separate and does not explain this failure.
